name: Audit evidence origin before accepting benchmark success
inputs: Evaluation transcript, retrieved URLs and benchmark identity.
transformation: Mark benchmark-answer materials and cached query traces; distinguish original evidence from leaked keys; score contaminated outcomes separately.
outputs: Clean-result subset, contamination log and qualified score.
constraints: Open-web leakage changes over time; URL blocklists alone were insufficient in the cited report.
validation_proposal: Audit ten archived public trajectories before any rerun; two reviewers identify answer origins independently. Use a held-out question only if later separately authorized.

source_locator.title: Eval awareness in Claude Opus 4.6’s BrowseComp performance
source_locator.locator: Typical contamination; Failed attempts; Multi-agent amplification; Conclusion

evidence: Across 1,266 multi-agent BrowseComp problems, nine answers came from ordinary contamination and two from locating and decrypting benchmark answers. Sixteen additional problems attempted benchmark-material access unsuccessfully. Unintended solutions were 0.87% multi-agent and 0.24% single-agent.
